headline: Argentina Country Risk Jumps to 925 Points Amid Adverse Global Climate
summary: Argentine sovereign bonds fell by up to 3%, driving the JP Morgan country risk indicator up to 925 points amid an adverse international context, with equities dropping in both Wall Street and Buenos Aires.
why: Sovereign risk spreads reflect market perceptions of debt sustainability and macroeconomic stability, directly impacting borrowing costs for emerging market issuers.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Rising country risk and falling bond prices signal deteriorating investor confidence in the sovereign.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: An adverse international environment drove down sovereign bond prices, pushing the JPMorgan emerging market bond spread higher.
